newsitem.title: UK: NatWest, HSBC rise on "buy" advice.
newsitem.headline: NatWest, HSBC rise on "buy" advice.

text.p: Shares in banks NatWest and HSBC benefited from reiterated "buy" advice from broker Panmure Gordon on Monday.
Shares in NatWest were up 11-1/2p at 708p and HSBC was 13-1/2p higher at 13.07-1/2 stg by 0943 GMT.
David Poutney, banking analyst at Panmure Gordon, repeated his "buy" advice on the shares ahead of the sector's reporting season. He also raised Barclays from a "hold" to a "buy".
"Generally speaking I think the banks will have a good first quarter," he said, adding that he had a share target of 840p for NatWest, 14.00 stg for HSBC and 11.00 stg for Barclays.
"The reason for changing Barclays is a very strong chance of another share buyback with the figures," Poutney said.
"HSBC is still a good way of participating in the long-term growth in the Far East," he added. "It is a massively capitalised bank which should do very well."

Poutney said he had upgraded his profit forecast for NatWest ahead of results. For the current year he added 30 million stg to his forecast of 1.579 billion stg, and 40 million stg to his 1997 forecast of 2.004 billion stg. He noted that his revised forecasts were still below the consensus estimate.
